# THE LIVING CUBE

*The deck as a turnable three by three by three, and the one cell that never
leaves home. A working, still under its own name.*

## I · WHAT IT IS

Twenty-seven cards; twenty-seven cells. The cube is the deck given a body it
can be turned in, and the fit is not decorative. Sort the cells by how many of
their depths are moving and the pieces of a turning cube fall out exactly: one
core that never moves, six centres, twelve edges, eight corners. One, six,
twelve, eight, which is the same census the rosette draws as its shells.

The surface owns only the rite. The engine beneath it is pure and pinned
elsewhere, so the cube cannot drift: the mapping, the twelve moves, the
scramble, the reduced return, and the invariants are all held by tests.

## II · THE NAMESAKE

The cube's name comes from what it refuses to do. Under any scramble at all,
the Seed does not move, and neither do the six centres. A pin drives three
hundred random turns and checks that they are all still home afterwards.

So the deck can be shaken as hard as anyone likes and its still point stays
exactly where it was. That is the Nodus stated in a solid: the organising
centre cannot be touched by the flow it organises, only turned around.

## III · THE SIX GATES

The rite runs in six: approach, holding, the cast, witnessing, the return, and
the setting down. The cast is a declared word of quarter turns, so a scramble
can be replayed. The return is that word inverted and then reduced, which is
the piece worth noticing: the drift is retraced and whatever cancels is
removed, so the way home is shorter than the way out. What cancels was never
part of the journey.

## IV · WHAT IT STILL ASKS

Its own header says the working name stands until the true name is fixed last,
at the device's own pressure. That name has not been given.

Beyond the name, the open question is where it belongs: whether the cube earns
a room of its own or stays a working that the Wayfinder and the Astrolabe
borrow from. It is further along than most workings here, being already sealed
in its engine and its liturgy, and it is the one the architect has said
deserves further exploration.

## V · WHERE IT STANDS

[Open the living cube](/app/luminara-cube.html). The plan it was built from is
kept at `docs/THE_LIVING_CUBE_PLAN.md`.

## VI · PROVENANCE

*The device was planned and swept in a single arc in July 2026, engine first
and pinned before the rite was written. This chart entered the room on 19 July
2026, when the workings were given a shelf of their own, so that a working
instrument would stop being reachable only by those who knew its address. Every
claim here about what the cube conserves is held by its tests rather than by
this text. The name is not settled and this chart does not settle it. Nothing
here predicts, and nothing here prescribes.*
